net sales.heading: Revenue Recognition
net sales.text:
The Company recognizes revenue from product sales upon product delivery. All of its products are shipped either same day or overnight or through longer shipping terms to the customer and the customer takes title to product and assumes risk and ownership of the product when it is delivered. Shipping charges to customers and sales taxes collectible from customers, if any, are included in revenues.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During the year ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, sales from the Company’s largest customer amounted to 42 % and 52 % of total sales, respectively.

In addition, Gate Gourmet, the leading global provider of airline catering solutions and provisioning services for airlines, in partnership with igourmet, represented 14 % and 16 % of total consolidated sales for the year ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

We rely on a few key customers for most of our revenue and if we were to lose one or more of those clients and be unable to generate new sales to offset such loss, we may be forced to cease or curtail our operations.
Our ability to execute may also depend on our ability to obtain additional capital on acceptable terms, if needed.

We rely upon outside vendors and shippers for our specialty food products and interruption in the supply of our products or their failure to adhere to our quality standards may negatively impact our revenues.
Since our customers rely on us to deliver their orders typically within 24-72 hours, delivery delays could significantly harm our business.

Our ability to respond to these changes may depend on our ability to identify attractive offerings, source or develop them, and execute fulfillment and service requirements on a timely and cost-effective basis.

Our business depends on internal technology systems and third-party platforms that support core operations, including order management, inventory and warehouse processes, logistics coordination, product and pricing data management, and integrations with customers, vendors, and other partners, and we may have limited control over required technology interfaces.
We cannot predict if investors will find our common stock less attractive because we may rely on these exemptions.
We rely on trademarks, trade secrets, and other forms of intellectual property protections, however, these protections may not be adequate.
We rely on a combination of trademark, trade secret and other intellectual property laws in the United States.
We also rely on unregistered proprietary rights, including common law trademark protection.
Our ability to generate sufficient cash to service our indebtedness depends on many factors, some of which are not within our control.
Our ability to make payments on our indebtedness will depend on our ability to generate cash in the future.

As a result of these deficiencies and certain account reconciliation and review controls that were not effectively designed in fully mitigating the related risks, automated process- level and manual controls within the financial reporting cycles that rely on information generated from such financially relevant systems were not considered effective.
